title: I Printed the Recycle-Center Scale Ticket After They Tared With a Foot

parts.text: I rolled cardboard onto the public scale at 10:17 a.m. and attendant Bo rested a boot on the frame while taring. The posted rate said: TARE EMPTY. PRINT THE TICKET. NO FOOT. I was forty-one, household, holding a load that suddenly weighed less. Bo grinned. "Boots are empty." I photographed the boot, the display, and the rate sign. Then I asked for a reprint with the boot off. At 10:22 the floor lead asked why Bo's boot was on a tare still. I waited where the camera already was. If it is written, it can be applied to the person who wrote it.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The floor lead can see Bo's boot on the tare still against the no-foot sign.

social.video_title: He tared the cardboard with a boot on the frame — Part 1/2
social.description: Recycle center, a light ticket, and a rate sign he stands on. I asked for a reprint. Would you have photographed the boot?

parts.text: Bo called it a wobble until the lead asked for the still. I printed the reprint, the photo, and the sign. Weight restored. Bo tared empty and told the line boots were always about optics. Optics is a word attendants use when a boot exists. Scale policy now has a second line: BOOTS ARE NOT EMPTY. I keep the reprint. Bo stands on the floor. The scale finally looks like a scale, not a discount. I go back to being a person with a receipt. The second photo is for the person who will say they never saw the first.

social.description: Reprint, restored weight, and a second line. Was a wobble ever a foot?
